title: Exotic Smooth Structures and Milnor Spheres

items.title: Exotic smooth structure and exotic sphere
items.statement: A smooth manifold $X$ is an exotic smooth structure on a specified smooth manifold $Y$ when their underlying topological manifolds are homeomorphic and $X$ is not diffeomorphic to $Y$. An exotic smooth $n$-sphere is a closed connected smooth $n$-manifold homeomorphic, but not diffeomorphic, to the standard smooth $S^n$. An orientation is extra data when oriented classes are compared. This definition concerns the smooth category; a homotopy equivalence alone does not assert a homeomorphism.
items.strategy: The homeomorphism and diffeomorphism predicates fix the two categories. The exoticness assertion is proved below for concrete seven-spheres.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405
Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: Smooth homotopy sphere
items.statement: A smooth homotopy $n$-sphere is a closed connected smooth $n$-manifold $Σ$ equipped with a homotopy equivalence $Σ\simeq S^n$. An oriented homotopy sphere carries a chosen orientation. No topological Poincaré assertion is built into the definition.
items.strategy: The homotopy type supplies the homology and fundamental-group data used later; oriented connected sum uses the extra orientation.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537
John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Compact smooth manifolds have finite CW models under countable choice
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every compact smooth manifold, with boundary allowed, has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex. If its boundary is a supplied finite CW manifold, its collar may be retained in a finite relative CW model.
items.strategy: Assume ACω for collars, partitions and the handle-to-cell interfaces. Regard W as the collared triad (W;empty,∂W); for a closed W both faces are empty. Construct a smooth boundary-product function f0 from the collar and a partition of unity. Its differential is nonzero on a fixed boundary strip. Cover the compact complement of a smaller strip by finitely many coordinate charts with smaller compactly contained chart cores and bumps ρ_i equal to one near those cores and supported away from the boundary. The finitely many functions ρ_i x_i^j have differentials spanning T*W at every point of this compact core. For the finite-dimensional family f_t=f0+Σt_ijρ_i x_i^j, the universal differential section is transverse to the zero section on the core. The zero set is a smooth parameterized critical-point manifold; applying the Euclidean Sard theorem in its countably many charts gives parameters t arbitrarily near zero for which the parameter projection is regular, equivalently every critical point of f_t is nondegenerate. ACω supplies at most countably many chart/null-cover choices; no infinite sequence of perturbations or general full-AC relative-jet theorem is used. Choose t small enough to keep df nonzero on the remaining boundary strip. Compactness makes the isolated critical set finite. Finite disjoint critical-point bumps separate its critical values while preserving the collar and nondegeneracy. This gives the adapted excellent Morse function actually needed by the ACω handle-correspondence statement; do not invoke its full-AC existence dependency. Its finite handle decomposition starts at the empty incoming face. Applying the declared handle-to-cell lemma successively gives a finite absolute CW model; with an already supplied finite incoming face the identical argument gives the relative version. Empty and zero-dimensional manifolds have finite discrete models. This finite-parameter construction is a local Step3 proof obligation, not an authored proof body.

items.title: Connected sum preserves homotopy spheres
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge3$, the oriented connected sum of two oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres is again an oriented smooth homotopy $n$-sphere.
items.strategy: Excising a disk from either summand preserves homology below degree $n-1$ and makes the punctured homotopy sphere acyclic, with the relative disk fundamental class mapping to its boundary fundamental class. Mayer–Vietoris for the two punctured manifolds joined along $S^{n-1}$ yields the integral homology of $S^n$; van Kampen gives trivial fundamental group. Collapse the complement of an oriented disk to obtain a degree-one map to $S^n$, hence a homology isomorphism. Finite CW models and the simply connected homology Whitehead theorem make this a homotopy equivalence. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness. The degree-one collapse from the connected sum to S^n is explicit; its homology equivalence is checked by the punctured-sphere Mayer–Vietoris calculation. No generator-selection use of the full-AC absolute Hurewicz theorem occurs here.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: Connected sum descends to oriented h-cobordism classes
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, oriented connected sum of smooth homotopy $n$-spheres descends to oriented h-cobordism classes and is associative and commutative, with the standard sphere as identity.
items.strategy: Assume AC_omega. Given h-cobordisms W: Sigma_0 -> Sigma_1 and W': Sigma'_0 -> Sigma'_1, choose orientation-compatible small coordinate disks in each incoming and outgoing face, attach a product 1-handle in the incoming collars joining the two incoming faces and a second product 1-handle in the outgoing collars joining the two outgoing faces, and round the corners by smooth collar gluing; the resulting compact cobordism has ends Sigma_0#Sigma'_0 and Sigma_1#Sigma'_1. For each new end inclusion, the homotopy inverses of the two given face inclusions, chosen along the collar neighbourhoods to agree with the attaching identifications, extend over the 1-handles and glue with the collar flow to homotopy inverses, so both end inclusions are homotopy equivalences and the cobordism is an h-cobordism. Disk-choice independence and the interchange and regrouping of the collar-handle picture are obtained by isotoping the attaching data (centres joined by a path in the connected face with oriented frames transported; the finitely many disks already used can be avoided) and applying the local handle-isotopy lemma, whose later-handles clause transfers the diffeomorphism to the total cobordisms. Removing a disk from S^n leaves a disk, so S^n#Sigma is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to Sigma. This proves the stated laws without using the h-cobordism-to-diffeomorphism theorem.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537
John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: Orientation reversal is the connected-sum inverse
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, $\Sigma\#(-\Sigma)$ is oriented h-cobordant to $S^n$ for each oriented smooth homotopy $n$-sphere $\Sigma$.
items.strategy: For n≥5 choose a smoothly embedded disk Dⁿ in Σ and set P=Σ\int(Dⁿ). The homology sequence of (Σ,P), excision to (Dⁿ,Sⁿ⁻¹), and van Kampen show P is acyclic and simply connected; the declared finite model and simply connected homology-Whitehead criterion give contractibility. This is the punctured homotopy sphere used in Kervaire–Milnor Lemma 2.4, not an assertion about arbitrary disk complements. Form V=P×[0,1]. Its corners along ∂P×{0,1} are rounded using product collars. The oriented boundary consists of P at the two ends joined by ∂P×[0,1], which is precisely Σ#(−Σ) with the second copy oppositely oriented; V is contractible. Remove the interior of a small smoothly embedded (n+1)-disk to obtain C, whose other boundary face is Sⁿ. Excision identifies H*(C,Sⁿ) with H*(V,Dⁿ⁺¹)=0, so Sⁿ→C is a homology isomorphism. The boundary fundamental-class relation [Σ#(−Σ)]+[Sⁿ]=0 in H_n(C) then shows the other boundary inclusion also induces an isomorphism (C has H_n=Z and no other reduced homology). Van Kampen applied after reattaching the removed disk shows π₁(C)=π₁(V)=0, since Sⁿ is simply connected; both faces are simply connected. The compact smooth CW models and Whitehead make both inclusions homotopy equivalences. Thus C is an h-cobordism from Sⁿ to Σ#(−Σ), proving that orientation reversal is the inverse. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537
John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: The homotopy-sphere group Θ_n
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, let $\Theta_n$ be the set of oriented h-cobordism classes of oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres, with connected sum as addition, $[S^n]$ as zero, and $[-\Sigma]$ as the inverse of $[\Sigma]$. The preceding connected-sum and inverse lemmas establish that this is an abelian group.
items.strategy: Under ACω, the connected-sum lemma proves the operation is well-defined and associative/commutative with identity, and the orientation-reversal lemma proves inverses. These verified laws give the stated abelian group structure.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: H-cobordism of homotopy spheres equals oriented diffeomorphism
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge5$, two oriented smooth homotopy $n$-spheres are oriented h-cobordant if and only if they are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. Thus the underlying classes of $\Theta_n$ can be read as oriented diffeomorphism classes.
items.strategy: An oriented diffeomorphism gives the product h-cobordism. Conversely an oriented h-cobordism has dimension $n+1\ge6$ and simply connected closed boundary faces, since each is a homotopy sphere. The smooth simply connected h-cobordism theorem, with its $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ premise, gives a product relative to one face; its other face is therefore oriented diffeomorphic to the first.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537
John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: Parallelizable bounds define a subgroup
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For n≥5, when Θₙ is the oriented homotopy-sphere group, its classes represented by boundaries of compact oriented parallelizable smooth (n+1)-manifolds form a subgroup.
items.strategy: Use oriented diffeomorphism to change boundary markings without changing a parallelizable filling. Attach a product 1-handle between boundary coordinate disks whose embeddings extend to larger disks; use the published smooth-handle attachment and collar interfaces. The exposed cylinder gives the oriented connected-sum boundary. Locally make positive tangent frames agree with the handle frame on neighborhoods of the feet and their edges, then restrict the glued ambient frames after corner rounding. Opposite orientation and the disk provide inverse and identity.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: The subgroup bP_{n+1}
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The subgroup $bP_{n+1}\subseteq\Theta_n$ consists of oriented homotopy-sphere classes represented by boundaries of compact oriented parallelizable smooth $(n+1)$-manifolds. Parallelizable means $TV$ is trivial; stably parallelizable means $TV\oplus\varepsilon^r$ is trivial for some $r$, which is weaker. The preceding lemma proves representative independence and subgroup closure.
items.strategy: Under ACω, the preceding lemma proves the boundary property is independent of the representative and that these classes form a subgroup.

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: Stable parallelizability of homotopy spheres (recorded, not proved here)

references.title: Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504-537
references.locator: Theorem 3.1 and its surrounding section, printed pp. 508-509, stable parallelizability of homotopy spheres

external_dependency.exact_statement:
Every smooth homotopy sphere is stably parallelizable: for a smooth homotopy
$n$-sphere $\Sigma$ there is an $r\ge0$ with
$T\Sigma\oplus\varepsilon^r\cong\varepsilon^{n+r}$.
external_dependency.local_proof_attempt: No local proof is supplied. Completed batch-24 adjudication identifies Bott stable SO groups, the signature theorem in dimensions divisible by four, and Adams injectivity of the stable J-homomorphism in residues 1 and 2 modulo 8 as inputs of the source proof. The needed all-dimension Bott and J prerequisite chain is not locally supplied; the concrete seven-dimensional disk-bundle calculation does not replace it.
external_dependency.necessity: Retained for mathematical orientation on the exotic-sphere page. It describes the general stable tangent-bundle property of homotopy spheres. No local construction, exoticness detector or group-closure proof uses this recorded claim as a prerequisite.

items.statement:
Every smooth homotopy sphere is stably parallelizable: for a smooth homotopy
$n$-sphere $\Sigma$ there is an $r\ge0$ with
$T\Sigma\oplus\varepsilon^r\cong\varepsilon^{n+r}$.
items.strategy: The proof is **not supplied here**. Its all-dimension argument requires Bott stable $SO$ groups, the signature input in dimensions divisible by four, and Adams injectivity of the stable $J$-homomorphism in the relevant residue classes. The necessary Bott and $J$ chain has no proved local supplier. The concrete Milnor disk-bundle calculations on this page do not establish this general result.

items.title: Quaternionic clutching bundles over S⁴
items.statement: Identify the oriented fibre $\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb H$ in the ordered basis $(1,i,j,k)$ and $S^3$ with unit quaternions. Give $S^4=D^4_+\cup_{S^3}D^4_-$ the orientation whose equatorial clutching-degree convention sends $u\mapsto(v\mapsto uv)$ and $u\mapsto(v\mapsto vu)$ to Euler number $+1$; let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be its positive generator. For integers $h,j$, $\xi_{h,j}$ is the oriented real rank-four bundle obtained by $(a,v)_+\sim(a,g_{h,j}(a)v)_-$, $g_{h,j}(a)v=a^hva^j$. Unit quaternion multiplication makes this a smooth norm-preserving oriented clutching map for every integer exponent.
items.strategy: Bundle existence and the upper-to-lower transition convention are supplied by clutching. The Euler-degree calibration and independence of the two basic maps are justified in subsequent local lemmas.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Euler number from the clutching obstruction
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from the Euler-class supplier. For an oriented rank-four bundle over $S^4$ clutched by $g:S^3\to SO(4)$, evaluation of the Euler class on $[S^4]$ is the degree of $a\mapsto g(a)v_0/\|v_0\|$, with the equatorial and fibre orientations fixed in the definition. For the basic left and right quaternion multiplications this degree is $+1$.
items.strategy: Trivialize over the upper disk and choose the constant nonzero section $v_0=1$. On the lower equator its boundary value is $g(a)1$; the obstruction to extending a nowhere-zero section over the lower disk is its degree. The local Euler obstruction/zero-count characterization identifies this obstruction with the Euler evaluation. Both $a1$ and $1a$ are the identity map of the oriented equator $S^3$, so both degrees are $+1$.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Pontryagin calibration of left and right quaternionic clutching
items.statement: Assume AC. With the preceding clutching, base and fibre orientations, the left multiplication bundle has $e=u$ and $p_1=2u$, while the right multiplication bundle has $e=u$ and $p_1=-2u$.
items.strategy: Right multiplication by $i$ commutes with left multiplication by every unit quaternion and gives a complex structure whose complex-oriented real basis is $(1,i,j,-k)$, opposite the stipulated quaternionic orientation. Left multiplication by $i$ commutes with right multiplication and gives complex basis $(1,i,j,k)$, agreeing with that orientation. For a complex rank-two bundle $V$, the $\pm i$ eigenspaces of its complexified complex structure give $(V_{\mathbb R})_{\mathbb C}\cong V\oplus\bar V$. Since $H^2(S^4)=0$, the Whitney and conjugation formulas yield $c_2((V_{\mathbb R})_{\mathbb C})=2c_2(V)$ and $p_1(V_{\mathbb R})=-2c_2(V)$. Top Chern equals Euler in the complex orientation, so the left bundle has $c_2=-e=-u$ and the right has $c_2=e=u$. This proves the two signed Pontryagin values.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Degree-four characteristic numbers add under clutching product
items.statement: Assume AC. For based clutching maps $g,g\prime:S^3\to SO(4)$, the Euler and first Pontryagin evaluations of the bundle clutched by their pointwise product are the sums of the corresponding evaluations for $g$ and $g\prime$. Inverse clutchings negate these evaluations.
items.strategy: The group structure on $\pi_3(SO(4))$ is represented by pointwise multiplication because $SO(4)$ is a topological group. The pinch $S^4\to S^4\vee S^4$ models addition of the two classifying maps. Naturality of universal characteristic classes and the coproduct $[S^4]\mapsto([S^4],[S^4])$ make every degree-four evaluation additive. A null clutching has trivial degree-four classes, so the inverse class has opposite evaluation.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Euler and first Pontryagin classes of ξ_{h,j}
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the fixed quaternionic, base, and upper-to-lower clutching orientations, $e(\xi_{h,j})=(h+j)u$ and $p_1(\xi_{h,j})=2(h-j)u$.
items.strategy: The map $g_{h,j}$ is the commuting pointwise product of $h$ copies of left multiplication and $j$ copies of right multiplication, interpreted through inverse maps for negative exponents. The previous two lemmas give Euler coefficients $h+j$ and Pontryagin coefficients $2h-2j$, with no remaining unspecified sign.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor sphere and disk bundles
items.statement: Give $\xi_{h,j}$ its Euclidean metric preserved by quaternionic clutching. Put $W_{h,j}=D(\xi_{h,j})$ and $M_{h,j}=S(\xi_{h,j})=\partial W_{h,j}$, with the disk bundle oriented by oriented base followed by oriented fibre and the sphere bundle carrying the induced boundary orientation. Then $S^3\to M_{h,j}\to S^4$ is a smooth sphere bundle, and $W_{h,j}$ is an explicit compact oriented smooth filling.
items.strategy: Norm-preserving gluing makes the unit sphere and closed disk bundles well-defined smooth manifolds; collaring of the fibre boundary supplies the displayed boundary identification.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Euler number ±1 gives an integral homology seven-sphere
items.statement: Assume AC. If $h+j=\pm1$, then $H_k(M_{h,j};\mathbb Z)\cong H_k(S^7;\mathbb Z)$ for every $k$, including the torsion assertion: only $H_0$ and $H_7$ are $\mathbb Z$.
items.strategy: The integral Gysin sequence of the oriented $S^3$ bundle has only the potentially nontrivial connecting map $H^0(S^4)\xrightarrow{\smile e}H^4(S^4)$, multiplication by $h+j$. This is an isomorphism when $h+j=\pm1$, so intermediate cohomology vanishes and top cohomology is $\mathbb Z$. Poincaré duality and the universal coefficient theorem for the closed oriented seven-manifold transfer this to integral homology without leaving hidden torsion.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor sphere bundles are simply connected
items.statement: Every $M_{h,j}$ is simply connected, in particular those with Euler number $\pm1$.
items.strategy: The fibre $S^3$ and base $S^4$ are path connected and simply connected. The homotopy long exact sequence contains $\pi_1(S^3)\to\pi_1(M_{h,j})\to\pi_1(S^4)$; both outside groups vanish, so the middle group vanishes.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor Euler ±1 bundles are homotopy seven-spheres
items.statement: Assume AC inherited from the Gysin calculation. If $h+j=\pm1$, $M_{h,j}$ is a smooth homotopy seven-sphere.
items.strategy: A degree-one map $S^7\to M_{h,j}$ represents its fundamental class by the simply connected Hurewicz theorem. It induces an isomorphism in every integral homology group by the preceding homology calculation, and both spaces have finite CW models. Homology Whitehead makes the map a homotopy equivalence. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness. Under its already stated AC, apply absolute Hurewicz successively in degrees 2 through 7: each lower homology vanishing forces the next homotopy group to vanish, and the degree-seven isomorphism supplies the generator map. Mere simple connectivity alone would not justify applying Hurewicz in degree seven.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Two-disk complement is an h-cobordism
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $d\ge6$, removing interiors of two disjoint smoothly embedded closed $d$-disks from a smooth homotopy $d$-sphere gives a compact simply connected h-cobordism between two standard $S^{d-1}$ boundary faces.
items.strategy: Van Kampen applied to each disk collar shows the complement is simply connected because the disks and boundary spheres are simply connected. Excision and the homology long exact sequence of the two removed disks show each boundary inclusion induces an integral homology isomorphism; equivalently use Mayer–Vietoris for adding back one disk at a time. Compact smooth manifolds have finite CW type. The simply connected homology Whitehead theorem upgrades each inclusion to a homotopy equivalence, exactly the h-cobordism condition. Use the preceding local compact-manifold finite-CW lemma under ACω to supply actual finite CW homotopy models before comparison. Transport the homology map along these supplied equivalences; the exact published simply connected homology-Whitehead example applies by its choice-free finite-CW clause, whose relative Hurewicz induction proves weak equivalence before finite Whitehead. The bare Whitehead theorem is not itself a homology-equivalence theorem. No finite CW type is inferred merely from compactness.

references.title: John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: Alexander extension over a disk
items.statement: Any homeomorphism $f:S^{d-1}\to S^{d-1}$ extends to a homeomorphism $F:D^d\to D^d$ by $F(0)=0$ and $F(rx)=rf(x)$ for $0<r\le1$. The extension need not be smooth at the origin.
items.strategy: The displayed formula is continuous for $r>0$. At $0$, $\|F(rx)\|=r$ uniformly in $x$, proving continuity. Its inverse is the identical radial construction from $f^{-1}$, so $F$ is a homeomorphism.

references.title: John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: Milnor homotopy seven-spheres are topological spheres
items.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $h+j=\pm1$, $M_{h,j}$ is homeomorphic to $S^7$.
items.strategy: Remove two disks from the homotopy seven-sphere. The complement is a simply connected seven-dimensional h-cobordism with boundary faces S⁶; it meets the smooth h-cobordism theorem threshold 7≥6. The theorem makes it a smooth cylinder. Reattach the two seven-disks to its ends. One attaching map may be a nonextendable boundary diffeomorphism, but Alexander’s radial extension gives a homeomorphism of the disk; the resulting topological manifold is S⁷. Full AC is inherited from the homology-sphere supplier, and AC implies the h-cobordism supplier’s ACω.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405
John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9, 109–110

items.title: Relative Kronecker evaluation is well-defined and natural
items.statement: For every pair (X,A), abelian coefficient group G and integer k, relative Kronecker evaluation H^k(X,A;G) × H_k(X,A;Z) → G is well-defined, biadditive, coefficient-compatible and natural for maps of pairs. For a commutative unital ring R, R-linear cochains and chains instead give the R-bilinear pairing H^k(X,A;R) × H_k(X,A;R) → R, with the same naturality.
items.strategy: Represent a relative cochain by a cochain vanishing on simplices in A and a relative cycle z by a chain with ∂z in C(A). Changing z by ∂b+c_A changes evaluation by δα(b)+α(c_A)=0; changing α by δβ changes it by β(∂z)=0. These equations also give bilinearity and naturality. This is the explicit relative contract needed for the pair evaluation maps; the class-level absolute Kronecker supplier alone does not state it. The abelian-group convention uses integral relative chains, as in the exact absolute supplier; the same-ring version uses R-linear cochains on R-chains. No multiplication on an arbitrary abelian group G is assumed.

items.title: Relative middle cup products are symmetric
items.statement: For any pair (X,A), the relative degree-four cup product H⁴(X,A;R) × H⁴(X,A;R) → H⁸(X,A;R) is symmetric.
items.strategy: Use the specified natural chain homotopy H between the Alexander–Whitney diagonal and its factor reversal. Naturality under A→X preserves C(A)⊗C(A), so the cochain primitive in the absolute graded-commutativity proof vanishes on A and descends to relative cochains. Since both degrees are four, the sign is positive. Forgetting either relative factor gives the corresponding relative/absolute symmetry. This supplies the relative symmetry used in the boundary form.

items.title: Relative cap product evaluation identity
items.statement: For a relative cohomology class a∈H^p(W,M;R), an absolute class x∈H^{n-p}(W;R), and the relative fundamental class [W,M], one has ⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩=⟨x,a∩[W,M]⟩ in the cohomology-first convention.
items.strategy: On each singular n-simplex the cap product evaluates a on the front p-face and x on the back (n−p)-face. The resulting cap chain is absolute by the relative cap definition. The cap boundary identity and vanishing of a on M make the chain-level evaluation descend to the relative class. The displayed convention has no extra sign. This is the explicit evaluation bridge used with Poincaré–Lefschetz duality.

items.title: Collared gluing gives relative excision and evaluation maps
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let W,W′ be compact oriented smooth eight-manifolds glued along an orientation-preserving identification of their common boundary M, and N=W∪_M(−W′). There are natural excision isomorphisms H*(N,V)≅H*(W,M), H*(N,U)≅H*(W′,M), and corresponding relative homology maps. Under them [N] restricts to [W,M] on the first side and to −[W′,M] on the second, compatibly with Kronecker evaluation and relative products.
items.strategy: Assume ACω for the collar-gluing supplier. Use the collar theorem and smooth gluing/corner-smoothing to form N. In a seam collar M×(−2a,2a), take U=int(W)∪M×(−2a,a) and V=int(W′)∪M×(−a,2a). Each retracts onto its filling and U∩V is the overlap collar. Explicit monotone collar-height homotopies give pair equivalences (U,U∩V)≃(W,M) and (V,U∩V)≃(W′,M). Since the complement of U in N is closed and contained in open V, excision in cohomology gives H*(N,V)≅H*(U,U∩V)≅H*(W,M); likewise for the other side and in homology. Naturality of relative products gives the product comparison. The image of [N] is identified with [W,M] by its local orientation at interior points and the collar boundary-local-homology lemma; on W′ the ambient orientation is reversed, giving −[W′,M]. Pair components lying entirely in one side use absolute relative pairs and the same componentwise argument. Do not extend arbitrary singular cochains by zero across the seam: cover-small excision supplies the chain maps.

items.title: Compact oriented boundary manifolds have finite-dimensional cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. If W is a compact oriented smooth manifold with boundary and F is a field, then every H^k(W;F) and H^k(W,∂W;F) is finite-dimensional.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from Poincaré–Lefschetz duality and the finite-generation supplier. Double W across a collar to a closed oriented manifold D(W); folding the second copy back gives a retraction D(W)→W, so H_*(W;Z) is a direct summand of the finitely generated homology of D(W). The integral groups are finitely generated. The field UCT identifies cohomology with Hom of finite-dimensional field homology (the Ext term vanishes because vector spaces are free under AC); Poincaré–Lefschetz duality gives the relative groups. This supplies finite-dimensionality without invoking a triangulation theorem.

items.title: Integral middle cohomology vanishing implies real middle cohomology vanishing
items.statement: Assume AC. For a closed oriented seven-manifold M, if H³(M;Z)=H⁴(M;Z)=0, then H³(M;R)=H⁴(M;R)=0.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Integral finite generation makes each H_k(M;Z) finitely generated. Apply the universal coefficient short exact sequence with coefficients Z: vanishing H^k implies Hom(H_k,Z)=0, so H_k has zero free part and is finite. With coefficients R, Hom(H_k,R)=0 and Ext(H_{k−1},R)=0, since multiplication by every nonzero integer is onto R. Thus the real cohomology in degrees 3 and 4 vanishes. The finite cyclic resolution verifies the Ext assertion; no integral-to-real substitution is left implicit.

items.title: Disk-bundle Thom class pairs with the base generator
items.statement: Assume AC. Let ξ be an oriented rank-four bundle over oriented S⁴ with Euler number ε=±1, W=D(ξ), M=S(ξ), x=π*u, and U the oriented Thom generator. With total orientation base followed by fiber and the induced boundary orientation, ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1.
items.strategy: Assume AC as required by the Thom, normal-Thom, and duality suppliers. Double W across its collar. The zero section is a closed oriented embedded S⁴ in the double, with normal bundle ξ; the Thom class supported on the W side maps under the excision map to the Poincaré dual of the zero section. Since j(U)=εx, x has relative lift εU, and its restriction to the zero section is u. The closed cap/evaluation identity therefore gives ⟨j_VE_W(U)∪L_W(x),[D(W)]⟩=⟨u,[S⁴]⟩=1. The collar evaluation comparison identifies the left side with ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩. Rank four makes the base/fiber block swap orientation-preserving; this checks the sign. This is the boundary comparison needed before using a Thom normalization in the Pontryagin calculation.

items.title: Tangent bundle of the Milnor disk bundle has the stable splitting
items.statement: Assume AC. For W=D(ξ_{h,j}) with projection π:S⁴←W, the stable tangent bundle satisfies TW⊕ε¹≅π*(ξ_{h,j}⊕ε⁵), and p₁(TW)=2(h−j)π*u under the calibrated clutching convention.
items.strategy: Assume AC for the vector-bundle connection and Pontryagin-class suppliers. The vertical tangent bundle is π*ξ and the quotient of TW by it is π*TS⁴. A smooth connection gives horizontal lifts and splits this exact sequence, so TW≅π*(TS⁴⊕ξ). The explicit map (v,t)↦v+tb identifies TS⁴⊕ε¹ with ε⁵. Hence TW⊕ε¹≅π*(ξ⊕ε⁵). Pontryagin naturality and stability reduce p₁(TW) to π*p₁(ξ)=2(h−j)π*u. This route uses no unproved Whitney cross-term cancellation.

items.title: Relative middle form and signature for an eight-manifold with boundary
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. For a compact oriented smooth eight-manifold $W$ with boundary $M$, let $I=\operatorname{im}(H^4(W,M;\mathbb R)\to H^4(W;\mathbb R))$. A relative lift $\tilde x$ of $x\in I$ defines $Q_W(x,y)=\langle\tilde x\smile y,[W,M]\rangle$. The relative pairing lemma below proves that this is independent of lift, symmetric, and nondegenerate on $I$ after quotienting its radical; define $\sigma(W)$ as the inertia signature of that quotient. This is distinct from the closed-manifold signature of the batch-12 definition.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Define A=H⁴(W,M;R), B=H⁴(W;R), j:A→B and I=im(j); set T(a,x)=⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩. PL duality together with the relative cap/evaluation identity and field UCT gives a perfect pairing A×B. The local finite-dimensionality lemma supplies finite-dimensionality. The formula Q_W(ja,y)=T(a,y) is independent of the lift because a change by ker(j) pairs trivially with I, by exactness/naturality and relative middle-degree symmetry. The same symmetry makes Q symmetric. Perfectness implies the form on I is nondegenerate (so its radical quotient is unchanged); define σ(W) as its inertia signature. This boundary definition is distinct from batch 12’s closed-manifold form.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405
Michel Kervaire and John Milnor, Groups of Homotopy Spheres I, Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), 504–537

items.title: Boundary middle form and Novikov gluing
items.statement: Assume AC. The relative middle form in the preceding definition is well-defined and symmetric on its nonsingular image quotient. If $W,W\prime$ are compact oriented eight-manifolds with identified oriented boundary $M$ satisfying $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$, then $N=W\cup_M(-W\prime)$ is closed oriented and $\sigma(N)=\sigma(W)-\sigma(W\prime)$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Work over R and put A=H⁴(W,M;R), B=H⁴(W;R), I=im(j), T(a,x)=⟨a∪x,[W,M]⟩. PL duality, the relative cap/evaluation identity, and field UCT give a perfect pairing A×B; finite dimensionality follows from the declared compact-boundary finite-dimensionality lemma. If ja=0, then T(a,jb)=T(b,ja)=0 for all b by relative symmetry, so lift changes pair trivially with I. This proves Q_W is well-defined and symmetric. If x=ja∈I is radical, T(a,jb)=0 for every b, hence T(b,x)=0 for every b; perfectness forces x=0. Thus the image form is already nondegenerate and quotienting its radical leaves it unchanged. Integral H³,H⁴ vanishing implies real vanishing by the declared UCT bridge. For two fillings, the collar/excision/evaluation lemma and MV identify H⁴(N;R) with the two filling groups and identify its closed middle form with Q_W⊕(−Q_W′). Sylvester inertia gives σ(N)=σ(W)−σ(W′). This proves the whole stated scope; the closed signature definition is not being applied directly to W.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Disk-bundle middle form and signature
items.statement: Assume AC. For $h+j=\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, the middle relative form of $W_{h,j}$ is the rank-one form $[\varepsilon]$ generated by the zero section, and $\sigma(W_{h,j})=\varepsilon$. For arbitrary $h,j$, the zero section has self-intersection $h+j$; when this is zero the homological zero-section form is degenerate, while the relative cohomological image I is zero, so its signature is zero.
items.strategy: Assume AC. The disk bundle retracts onto the oriented zero section S⁴, so its middle absolute cohomology is generated by x=π*u. The zero section has normal bundle ξ_{h,j}; batch 2 self-intersection equals Euler gives square h+j in the boundaryless interior. The relative calculation is explicit: j(U)=εx by the Euler pullback formula, the new Thom/base evaluation lemma gives ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1, and relative/mixed symmetry identifies the image form on x with Q_W(x,x)=ε. For ε=±1 it is the nonsingular rank-one form [ε], with signature ε. When h+j=0, the rank-one homological zero-section form is zero, but j(U)=0 makes the cohomological image I zero-dimensional; its image form is already nonsingular on the zero space and has signature zero. Do not call this image a degenerate rank-one form. Thus the boundary-form comparison, rather than the closed ambient intersection theorem alone, justifies the assertion.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Relative square equals mixed evaluation
items.statement: Let $j:H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)\to H^4(W;\mathbb Z)$ and $a\in H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)$. Then $\langle a\smile a,[W,M]\rangle=\langle a\smile j(a),[W,M]\rangle$, where the left product uses two relative factors and the right uses one relative and one absolute factor.
items.strategy: Let a be represented by a relative cocycle α on (W,M), so α vanishes on every simplex in M. In the both-relative product take A=B=M; each is open in A∪B=M and C(M)+C(M)=C(M), so the quotient comparison in the relative cup definition is the identity. In the relative/absolute product take A=M,B=∅; its comparison is also the identity. Thus both a∪a and a∪j(a) are represented by exactly α∪α in C⁸(W,M), and their evaluations on [W,M] agree. The relative evaluation pairing is well-defined by the declared local lemma: changing a relative cycle by ∂b+c_M or a cocycle by δβ changes evaluation by zero. This proves the equality directly, without interpreting a boundary square as an absolute degree-eight evaluation.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Relative Pontryagin square of a Milnor disk bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. If $h+j=\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ and $k=h-j$, then the unique relative lift $\bar p_1\in H^4(W_{h,j},M_{h,j};\mathbb Z)$ of $p_1(TW_{h,j})$ exists and $q(W_{h,j}):=\langle\bar p_1\smile\bar p_1,[W_{h,j},M_{h,j}]\rangle=4\varepsilon k^2$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Put ε=h+j=±1, k=h−j, x=π*u, and let U be the oriented Thom generator. The tangent splitting lemma gives p₁(TW)=2kx. The Thom theorem identifies H⁴(W,M)=ZU and H⁴(W)=Zx; Euler pullback gives j(U)=εx, so the unique relative lift is bar p₁=2kεU. The disk-bundle Thom/base evaluation lemma proves ⟨U∪x,[W,M]⟩=1 with the base-followed-by-fiber orientation. The relative-square/mixed-evaluation lemma then gives q(W)=⟨bar p₁²,[W,M]⟩=⟨(2kεU)∪(2kx),[W,M]⟩=4εk². The integrality and ε=±1 hypothesis are essential.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor lambda candidate from a supplied filling
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth seven-manifold with $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$, and let $W$ be a supplied compact oriented smooth eight-manifold with $\partial W=M$. The pair sequence makes $j:H^4(W,M;\mathbb Z)\to H^4(W;\mathbb Z)$ an isomorphism. Define $\bar p_1(W)=j^{-1}p_1(TW)$, $q(W)=\langle\bar p_1(W)\smile\bar p_1(W),[W,M]\rangle$, and the filling-level candidate $\lambda_W(M)=2q(W)-\sigma(W)\pmod7$. This definition asserts no general existence of $W$ and no independence of $W$; both are separate questions. For disconnected fillings, define p1(TW) as the unique class restricting to the supplied first Pontryagin class on each of the finitely many compact path-connected components; for empty W it is zero.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Let M be closed oriented seven-dimensional with integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0, and let a compact oriented filling W be supplied. The pair-sequence segment H³(M)→H⁴(W,M)→H⁴(W)→H⁴(M) proves that j is an integral isomorphism: H³=0 gives uniqueness, H⁴=0 gives existence. Define bar p₁=j⁻¹p₁(TW), q(W)=⟨bar p₁∪bar p₁,[W,M]⟩, and λ_W=2q(W)−σ(W) mod 7 using the boundary-form definition. The relative-square/mixed-evaluation lemma validates the relative product evaluation. This is conditional on a supplied bound and asserts neither a universal bounding theorem nor filling independence.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Relative Pontryagin squares glue to the closed Pontryagin number
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the hypotheses of the lambda-candidate definition for two fillings W,W′ of the same oriented M, let N=W∪_M(−W′). Then ⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩=q(W)−q(W′). Orientation reversal changes evaluation signs, not the Pontryagin class itself.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Let W,W′ fill the same M and N=W∪_M(−W′). The pair sequence segment H³(M)→H⁴(W,M)→H⁴(W)→H⁴(M), with both boundary groups zero, makes each relative-to-absolute map an integral isomorphism. MV on the explicit collar cover U,V gives H⁴(N)≅H⁴(W)⊕H⁴(W′). For x∈H⁴(W), excision extends its unique relative lift from (W,M) to (N,V), then forgets relative conditions to a class L_W(x) with restrictions (x,0); similarly L_W′(x′) has restrictions (0,x′). MV uniqueness shows p₁(TN)=L_W(p₁(TW))+L_W′(p₁(TW′)): the tangent charts glue across the seam with the normal coordinate reversed, giving a real bundle isomorphism, while p₁ is orientation-independent. Cross products vanish because the extended factors lie in H⁸(N,U∪V)=H⁸(N,N)=0 via the excisive relative product; do not claim arbitrary singular cochains extended by zero are cochains. Same-side product naturality plus the relative excision/evaluation lemma gives the W evaluation q(W), and −q(W′) on the oppositely oriented second half. Expanding the square therefore yields ⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩=q(W)−q(W′). This is a complete local route; the actual item body still needs authoring.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor lambda is an oriented boundary invariant modulo seven
items.statement: Assume AC. For a closed oriented smooth seven-manifold $M$ with $H^3(M;\mathbb Z)=H^4(M;\mathbb Z)=0$ and at least one supplied compact oriented smooth eight-dimensional filling, $\lambda(M):=2q(W)-\sigma(W)\in\mathbb Z/7$ is independent of the filling and invariant under orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphism. Reversing the orientation of $M$ negates $\lambda(M)$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. For two supplied fillings glue N=W∪_M(−W′). The relative Pontryagin-square comparison gives q(W)−q(W′)=⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩, and the boundary-form gluing lemma gives σ(W)−σ(W′)=σ(N). Batch 12’s closed eight-dimensional formula, applied only to closed N, says 45σ(N)=7⟨p₂(TN),[N]⟩−⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩. Modulo 7, 3σ+p₁²=0, so p₁²=4σ and 2p₁²−σ=0. Substitution proves λ_W=λ_W′. An orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphism transports a filling with collars and preserves this comparison. Reversing orientation negates fundamental-class evaluations and signature while fixing p₁, hence negates λ. No filling existence for every M is asserted.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Milnor’s exotic seven-sphere
items.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. $M_{2,-1}$ is homeomorphic to $S^7$ but is not diffeomorphic to it. More generally, for $h+j=1$, the constructed sphere has $\lambda(M_{h,j})=(h-j)^2-1\pmod7$; a nonzero value obstructs a diffeomorphism to the standard sphere even without a prescribed orientation.
items.strategy: Assume AC. For ε=h+j=1 and k=h−j, the disk-bundle relative Pontryagin calculation gives q=4k² and its boundary form gives σ=1, so λ=8k²−1≡k²−1 mod 7. At (h,j)=(2,−1), k=3 and λ=8≡1; the standard sphere bounds D⁸ with q=σ=0. The lambda theorem makes this an obstruction to an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. If an orientation-reversing diffeomorphism existed, the standard sphere’s zero invariant would still be zero under negation, contradicting λ=1. Separately, the homology/Gysin and Whitehead steps give a homotopy sphere; its two-disk complement is a seven-dimensional h-cobordism between S⁶ ends, within dimension≥6, so the batch-15 h-cobordism theorem gives a cylinder and the radial Alexander extension supplies a homeomorphism after reattaching disks. The topological recognition route is separate from the characteristic invariant.

title: Exotic Smooth Structures and Milnor Spheres — Examples

items.title: The quaternionic Hopf sphere bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. $M_{1,0}\cong S^7$ by the quaternionic Hopf fibration, with $e(\xi_{1,0})=u$, $p_1(\xi_{1,0})=2u$, and $\lambda(M_{1,0})=0$.
items.strategy: Write $S^7=\{(q_0,q_1)\in\mathbb H^2:|q_0|^2+|q_1|^2=1\}$ and map to $\mathbb HP^1\cong S^4$ by $[q_0:q_1]$. Over the two affine charts, the unit quaternion fibre coordinate changes by left multiplication by the normalized coordinate ratio; this is precisely the $(1,0)$ clutching after the chosen orientation of the equator. The class formula gives $e=u,p_1=2u$, and the disk-bundle computation gives $\lambda=1^2-1=0$.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Gysin calculation of a Milnor homology sphere
items.statement: Assume AC. For $(h,j)=(2,-1)$, the Euler map in the integral Gysin sequence is multiplication by $1$, so $H^0(M;\mathbb Z)=H^7(M;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and every intermediate group vanishes.
items.strategy: Insert $e=(2-1)u=u$ into the sequence $H^0(S^4)\xrightarrow{\smile u}H^4(S^4)$. It is an isomorphism; all other base cohomology outside degrees zero and four vanishes. The remaining degree-zero and degree-seven terms are $\mathbb Z$, exactly as stated.

items.title: Intersection matrix of a Milnor bound
items.statement: Assume AC. For $W_{2,-1}$ the zero-section middle form is the one-by-one matrix $[1]$, and $\sigma(W_{2,-1})=1$.
items.strategy: The normal bundle of the zero section is $\xi_{2,-1}$. Its Euler number is $2+(-1)=1$, which equals the self-intersection; hence the middle form has matrix $[1]$ and positive signature one.

references.title: John Milnor, On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere, Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), 399–405

items.title: Two distinct Milnor lambda values
items.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. $M_{1,0}$ and $M_{2,-1}$ are both homeomorphic to $S^7$ but have $\lambda=0$ and $\lambda=1\pmod7$, respectively, and therefore are not diffeomorphic.
items.strategy: The first has $h-j=1$, giving $1^2-1=0$. The second has $h-j=3$, giving $3^2-1=8\equiv1$. The boundary invariance theorem distinguishes even an unoriented diffeomorphism because orientation reversal fixes zero.

items.title: Topological type does not determine smooth type
items.statement: Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The standard $S^7$ and $M_{2,-1}$ are homeomorphic closed seven-manifolds but are not diffeomorphic. Thus homeomorphism type does not determine smooth structure in dimension seven.
items.strategy: The topological identification and nonzero lambda obstruction are established by the main Milnor theorem; the two structures form the claimed counterexample.
